name: Store privacy labels
plain: What LinkedIn tells Apple and Google it collects.
meaning: Self-reported lists, not audits. Differences between the two labels show how much each store lets a developer say.

android.note: Declares no data shared with third parties

ios.note: Declares Data Linked to You; Apple says unverified

limits.headline: Can tell you what LinkedIn says it collects, on its store pages
limits.user_action: You open the app page in the App Store or Google Play
can: Show a list of data LinkedIn says it collects
Show whether data is linked to you (iPhone) or shared with third parties (Android)
Show the lists side by side so you can compare stores
cannot: Prove the labels are true; they are self reported, and Apple says unverified
Show the same details on both, since each store has its own form
limits.reach_label: A label on the store page
limits.differs: Apple lists Data Linked to You. Google's Data safety section says no data is shared with third parties.

story.what_it_is: The lists LinkedIn gave Apple and Google about what data the app collects.

marketing.name: App Store listing for LinkedIn
marketing.pitch: The App Privacy section shows data linked to you and data used to track you.

story.for_you: You can read a list on each store page before you install. The two lists look different because each store asks different questions.
story.for_makers: They are self reported lists, not audits. The gaps between the two show how much each store lets a developer say.

use_cases.example: A user compares the two store labels and sees that iOS lists more data types.
A researcher checks the label against the real network traffic.
A reporter writes about how apps describe tracking differently.
A company reviews the label before allowing the app on work phones.
A parent uses the label to decide if a teen should install it.
A developer team updates the label after adding a new analytics tool.

story.android_note: Google Play's Data safety section lists collected data and sharing.
story.ios_note: Apple's App Privacy section lists data linked to you and used to track you.

linkedin.how: Play (15 Nov 2026): collects contacts, device IDs, calendar events, photos, videos, approximate location, app interactions, installed apps, web browsing history, health info, race and ethnicity, sexual orientation, voice recordings and more; shares nothing. Apple: Data Linked to You for purchases, financial info, coarse and precise location, contact info, contacts, user content, search history, identifiers, usage, diagnostics; no tracking section seen. Surfshark (Sept 2026) flagged browsing history on Android only.
